items.title: Hyundai Glovis plans Philadelphia terminal expansion and lease through 2056
items.summary: Yonhap's October 20 report, datelined Washington on October 19, confirms plans for a dedicated car-carrier berth, additional vehicle storage and a Philadelphia land lease through 2056. Planned capacity would rise from 33,600 to 37,600 vehicles. The report follows the October 13 port-expansion ceremony and updates the existing story; no monitored vessel is identified.

items.title: Hyundai Glovis fleet projected to reach 110 vessels by year-end
items.summary: Financial News cited Meritz Securities as projecting Hyundai Glovis's fleet to rise from 98 vessels at the end of the first half of 2026 to 110 by year-end and 120 by the end of 2027. The report concerns company-wide fleet capacity and does not identify any of the 44 monitored vessels.

items.title: Glovis Legend delivered for Hyundai Glovis operation
items.summary: Guangzhou Shipyard International delivered the 10,800-CEU LNG dual-fuel PCTC Glovis Legend on October 12, nearly nine months ahead of schedule. The HMM-owned ship will be operated by Hyundai Glovis and is outside the 44-vessel watchlist.

items.title: Hyundai Glovis extends HiNAS autonomous navigation to 10 newbuild PCTCs
items.summary: Avikus said Hyundai Glovis contracted HiNAS Control and Surround View Monitoring for 10 newbuild 10,800-CEU PCTCs, some already delivered and the remainder due through 2028. The rollout would bring the HiNAS-equipped fleet to 18 vessels; the source does not identify any of the 44 monitored ships.

items.title: Hyundai Glovis and LGL to study SMR-powered car carrier operations
items.summary: Hyundai Glovis and Liberty Global Logistics signed an agreement on September 30 to assess the commercial, regulatory and operational requirements for an SMR-powered PCTC service between South Korea and the United States. The project concerns a future vessel concept and none of the 44 monitored ships.

items.title: Hyundai Glovis targets 67% fixed fleet capacity by 2029
items.summary: A Daishin Securities report cited by ChosunBiz says Hyundai Glovis plans to raise the share of owned vessels and long-term charters from 47% in 2025 to 67% by 2029. The report concerns fleet procurement strategy rather than a specific monitored vessel.

items.title: New long-term car carrier charter for Hyundai Glovis
items.summary: Korea Shipping Corporation announced a 73 billion won charter with Hyundai Glovis, due to run from November for five years and four months. This concerns the wider operating fleet; the article does not identify one of the 44 monitored vessels.

items.title: SpaceX reviews Starlink operations aboard Glovis Stella
items.summary: Hyundai Glovis reported on August 19 that a SpaceX delegation visited Glovis Stella at Gwangyang to inspect Starlink equipment and hear crew feedback. The accompanying photograph dates the visit to August 5. Glovis Stella is one of the 44 monitored vessels.

items.title: Glovis Nova begins maiden voyage as Hyundai Glovis expands 10,800-CEU fleet
items.summary: Hansa reported that the newly delivered Glovis Nova, the third 10,800-CEU car carrier in Hyundai Glovis's new series, began its maiden voyage to Europe with a record vehicle cargo. The vessel is part of the wider operating fleet and is not one of the 44 monitored ships.

items.title: Glovis Lighthouse makes first European port call at Southampton
items.source: The Maritime Executive / Associated British Ports
items.summary: Glovis Lighthouse called at Southampton on July 14 during its maiden voyage, becoming the port's largest vehicle carrier by capacity. The 10,800-CEU ship belongs to the wider Hyundai Glovis operating fleet and is not one of the 44 monitored vessels.

items.title: Hyundai Glovis partners to verify remote navigation for car carriers
items.summary: Hyundai Glovis reported on June 8 that it signed a June 2 agreement at Posidonia with G-Marine Service, Avikus and Korean Register to develop and verify a remote-operation concept for car carriers. The project concerns operating procedures, technology and safety assessment; it does not establish crewless operation or identify any of the 44 monitored ships.

items.title: Hyundai Glovis signs Amsterdam vehicle-terminal partnership
items.summary: Koopman reported on June 2 that it, Hyundai Glovis and the Port of Amsterdam signed a strategic agreement in Amsterdam on May 28 to develop a dedicated finished-vehicle logistics terminal. The partnership covers maritime transport, storage and distribution. No monitored vessel is identified.

items.title: Glovis Sunlight supports ocean-plastic monitoring as partnership expands
items.summary: A May 21 report identifies an ADIS debris-imaging camera aboard Glovis Sunlight, one of the 44 monitored vessels. Hyundai Glovis said its Ocean Cleanup partnership would run through 2030 and reported 20 cameras on 10 car carriers. The renewal had already been announced by The Ocean Cleanup in April; the May report provides the named-vessel detail and expanded deployment figures.

items.title: Hyundai Glovis deploys 10,800-vehicle Glovis Leader
items.summary: Hyundai Glovis announced the deployment of Glovis Leader after its April 28 delivery. The LNG dual-fuel PCTC can carry 10,800 vehicles; it is part of the wider operating fleet and is not one of the 44 monitored vessels.

items.title: Middle East disruption forces Hyundai Glovis route changes
items.summary: Hyundai Glovis said on April 3 that some Middle East routes were inaccessible, requiring temporary cargo storage and diversions through hubs including Sri Lanka. Reuters did not identify any of the 44 monitored vessels.

items.title: First 10,800-CEU PCTC for HMM-Hyundai Glovis partnership floated out
items.summary: Guangzhou Shipyard International floated out the first 10,800-CEU vehicle carrier for the HMM-Hyundai Glovis partnership on January 21. The ship was subsequently named Glovis Leader and is outside the 44-vessel watchlist.

items.title: GTT selected for tank design of Hyundai Glovis LNG newbuild
items.summary: GTT announced a tank-design order for a 174,000 m3 LNG carrier to be built by Hyundai Samho for Hyundai Glovis, using Mark III Flex containment technology. Delivery is scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2028. The unnamed newbuild is outside the 44-vessel watchlist.

items.title: Hyundai Glovis secures KRW 580 billion long-term LNG shipping contract
items.summary: Hyundai Glovis announced on November 27, 2025 a contract with an unnamed global trading company expected to generate approximately KRW 580 billion over up to 15 years. A new 174,000 m3 LNG carrier was planned to serve US Gulf Coast-to-global routes from 2029. The report concerns an unnamed future vessel, not one of the 44 monitored ships.
